_note: What Ichiro, the charcoal burner of Sakurazaka, says when the farmer talks to him (Talk, README.md, Villagers): the first pick whose if holds names the lines, one of them by the day; gift_ lines answer a gift by its reaction, gift_items his own answers to a keepsake and to dishes; gift_birthday on his birthday (fall 9). The close lines from band 4, kiln lines once his band 5 scene is seen (heart_ichiro_5), dear lines at band 6 once his band 6 scene is seen (heart_ichiro_6). A man of few words. Our own lines.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: I took the day off from the axe. The grove gets one quiet day a year too.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Hot work by that yakisoba griddle. Still cooler than my kiln.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Roast chestnuts smell like the end of a good burn. Smells like home to me.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: That bonfire's good cedar. I split half of it myself, if anyone asks.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...Still here.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Talk's done. Wood isn't.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Ichiro. I burn charcoal. The village's fires, the smithy's forge. Mine, mostly.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Don't walk in the grove when I'm felling. Shout first.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Wet wood smokes and won't burn clean. I split indoors on days like this.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Oak makes the best charcoal. Bamboo's for the quick fires. Hachiro wants oak.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Take one tree, leave the stump. It comes back in fifteen years. My father's trees are mine now.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Fumi's rice balls. Best part of the day. Don't tell her I said so.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Winter's my busy time. Every house wants charcoal for the kotatsu. Good.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: The kiln's past the grove, up the hill. Too hot to visit. Too far, too.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: You farm. I burn. Both of us work with fire and dirt. Hm.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Miners come back black as me. Fumi makes them wash before tea.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Bamboo shoots in the grove. Dig them before they're knee high. After that they're wood.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Sansho on the creek bank, by the far pine, past my woodpiles. Mind the thorns.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Nameko by the pine below my house. Akebi past the woodpiles. Fumi likes akebi. Don't say who brings it.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Enoki by the far pine, past the grove. Only thing that grows in this cold. Like me.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...Who told you? Fumi. Hm. One day a year the axe rests. Today's it.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Tome has me hauling wood for the shrine fire. Three days. Fine. Wood I understand.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Fumi cried into the teapot when I told her. Then charged me for the tea. Hm.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Morning. Stove's lit. Oak, from the new kiln. It rings.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Off to the woods. Eat something. You forget, when it's sunny.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Your hens woke me. The kiln never did that. ...I don't mind.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Back. Washed, before you say anything. Mostly.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Long day? Sit. I'll split kindling for tomorrow. Quiet work.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Kotatsu's warm. The house smells of smoke now. Sorry. ...Not very sorry.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Watered the dry rows before the woods. Heavy can. Light work.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: The rows by the path were thirsty. Gave them a can. They'll live.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Filled the coop's feed box. The hens don't fear me. Odd. Everyone else does.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Feed's in the coop. From your sack. I counted the scoops.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Married. Still cut wood. Still smell of smoke. You knew that.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Fumi still packs my rice balls. Says it's for your sake, so I eat. Hm.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: On the day, too. ...Nobody's done that since my father. Thank you.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Left a sack of charcoal by your gate. Oak. Don't pay me. Just don't waste it.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: You walk heavier than when you came. Good. Means you're carrying things.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: The new kiln draws well. First burn rang like a bell. Three in ten, now. ...Four.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: I put a mark in the kiln's clay by the door. My father's, mine. Left room for one more.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Three marks on the kiln door. I touch them when I load it. Superstition. Don't laugh.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Every sack I fill, I set the best piece aside for your stove. The others get what's left. Don't tell them.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Fumi says I smile when you walk up. I don't. ...Hm. Maybe a little.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...That's good. Thank you. Really.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Hm. Thanks.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: I'll take it.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Too sweet. Give it to Fumi.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Clay? Clay cracks the kiln. Get it away from me.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: One's enough.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: A charm for safety. ...I'll hang it by the kiln door. Thank you.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Hot and heavy. That's a meal. I'll eat it now, standing.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Cooked food. Better than mine. Thanks.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Food is food.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Too soft. Too sweet. ...Fumi might like it.
